newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Fire disrupts Czech Metro, two people reported hurt.
newsitem.headline: Fire disrupts Czech Metro, two people reported hurt.

text.p: Fire broke out on Prague's underground railway network on Friday, the second blaze in the Metro in five days, the Czech news agency CTK reported.
Two Metro workers were taken to hospital suffering from smoke inhalation, it said.
On Monday, a fire was reported on the same A line and both incidents were believed to have been caused by by faults in high voltage electrical cables.
Friday's fire started at the Zelivskeho station at 4.10 am (0210 GMT), two hours before the rush hour, CTK said. Services were suspended for two and a half hours.

A Line is the second oldest of three lines on the electrically-driven Prague system, largely built by the communists and using Soviet-made trains. It has largely enjoyed a reputation as safe and efficient.
